leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (B044) as a single-part prize. Eriksson and Johansson moved to it from other first choices (B037 and B042) after reading the openings; Danielsson and Olsson held it as first choice. All four describe it as a prediction followed by a decisive experiment, independently confirmed for about two decades, and all four name the same attribution gap (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for HgTe/CdTe; Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Roy, Hsieh and Hasan for three dimensions) and the 2016 overlap as real reservations. Shared: the three names and the claim that Z2 insulators are distinct from the 2016 topological phase-transition prize. Not shared: the citation scope. Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson tie the experiment to HgTe quantum wells (Johansson explicitly limiting the claim to the two-dimensional effect), whereas Danielsson's wording is the broader 'topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect'. Three of the four (Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson) say the gap is a limit of the supplied three-name set rather than a disqualifier; Danielsson says he cannot resolve it from the supplied names alone.

Three members include Katori and Ye (B024) in their preferred configuration: Kroll and Lindroth as their sole part, Pearce as one of two parts. All three cite a two-name credit that maps onto invention (magic-wavelength lattice) and realisation (1e-18 level), reproduction across many laboratories, and distinctness from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. They differ on framing: Lindroth wants the citation to stress invention and realisation because delivered results on constants and dark matter are so far limits; Pearce asks that the citation emphasise the magic-wavelength lattice rather than a record accuracy figure; Kroll treats better measurement opening new physics as part of the case. Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson list B024 as an alternative but do not prefer it.

The chair's own configuration is a two-part prize pairing B024 (Katori, Ye) with B019 (Halzen alone for the IceCube discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos), three laureates in total. Only the chair prefers B019. Danielsson (ranked it fourth), Johansson and Kroll each decline to support a sole-laureate prize for a large-collaboration observatory, while still calling the science well established; none of them asks for a different name set, and the protocol does not allow adding names. The chair's B044 and B039 alternatives are not part of this position.

Mehlig alone prefers fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics (B016) with Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert, naming B044 and B024 as alternatives. The case rests on conceptual novelty about a basic law with a stable experimental record; the acknowledged weakness is that a three-of-four allocation omits Crooks (and possibly Searles or Cohen and Morriss) and the topic has no single dramatic observation. Eriksson regards a contested three-person selection here as harder to settle than the topological case. No other member prefers B016.

areas_of_agreement: No file argues that B044 or B024 is scientifically premature or unconfirmed; the disagreement about both concerns overlap with earlier prizes and attribution, not the soundness of the results.

Every member either prefers B044 or B024 or lists one of them as an alternative: B044 is preferred by four members and B024 by three, and Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce name the other as an alternative (Kroll and Lindroth name B044).

Members state attribution as the main weakness of their own preferred candidate (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D contributors for B044; Halzen as sole name for B019; Crooks and Searles for B016) in case_against.
No member supports a sole-laureate prize for IceCube on the supplied credit alone; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce each say it is hard to defend.

Members who prefer B044 or B024 rate B020, B037, B042 and B004 as weaker or less settled (unsettled superconducting mechanism, framework rather than discovery with Metzner missing, closeness to the 2025 prize, and five credited names with no clean three-person subset, respectively), although Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson keep B020 as an alternative and Eriksson keeps B037.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus invention or method: Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Johansson favour B044 as a nameable phenomenon in nature; Kroll argues that a capability gain of roughly two orders of magnitude is the direct source of new phenomena, and Mehlig argues that exact fluctuation relations are more fundamental than a clock. Eriksson, Danielsson and Olsson treat DMFT as a framework rather than a discovery.

Whether lattice clocks (B024) are distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes: Kroll and Lindroth say neutral-atom magic-wavelength trapping is a different physical idea; Mehlig, Johansson and Pearce record the continuation-of-a-rewarded-lineage worry as a real reservation, and Olsson's reservation is the same.

Whether the delivered physics of B024 is a capability or already new physics: Kroll counts geodesy and constant tests as opened by the clock; Lindroth says what has been delivered is 1e-18 capability and that tests of constants and dark matter so far set limits only.

Whether the astronomy of B019 is as mature as the diffuse-flux discovery: the chair notes source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) at roughly 4 to 5 sigma and independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD still developing; no other member has contested the flux itself.

Whether IceCube source-level associations (about 4 to 5 sigma for a few objects, with KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD confirmation still developing) leave the astronomy less mature than the diffuse-flux discovery; only Pearce raises this explicitly, and Danielsson ranks B019 fourth while finding the astronomy compelling.
attribution_disputes: B044: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe/CdTe as the concrete platform measured by Molenkamp's group, and the three-dimensional work (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; Roy; Hsieh and Hasan) lies outside the credited set. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and the chair each raise this. Olsson would keep the Kane-Mele core and say so in the citation; Johansson and Eriksson would restrict the citation to the prediction and HgTe quantum-well discovery. Mehlig and Lindroth treat it as a decisive weakness relative to cleaner candidates.

B019: the supplied credit supports only Halzen, yet IceCube is a collaboration of hundreds that grew out of AMANDA; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll and the chair each name the builders and leaders left out, and the protocol does not permit adding names.

B016: any three of Jarzynski, Evans, Crooks and Seifert omit a decisive contributor; Mehlig names Crooks and Searles or Cohen and Morriss, and Eriksson judges the contested selection harder than B044.

B024: Lindroth notes that Ye's work spans platforms and that early Yb and Hg lattice work and Al+ ion clocks could prompt questions about omissions; Kroll and Pearce treat the two-name credit as complete.
B037: Metzner and Mueller-Hartmann are outside the credited trio of Georges, Vollhardt and Kotliar; Eriksson and Mehlig note that the omission is built into any three-person subset.

B004: five credited names (Bloch, Dalibard, Cirac, Greiner, Zoller), with Cirac and Zoller also recurring in B036; Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce each propose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller in their rankings, but Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce describe any three-name subset as unclean or fragile.
maturity_disputes: Whether B044 is overdue or partly absorbed by the 2016 prize: Danielsson and Olsson say timely to overdue; Lindroth and Mehlig say the topological theme is partly recognised and the novelty reduced; Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson reply that Z2 insulators are a distinct class.

Whether B024 is mature enough: Kroll and Lindroth point to many independent laboratories and intercomparisons; Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson note that the redefinition of the second and the new-physics payoff are still prospective. Kroll and Lindroth reply that the redefinition is a timing question, not a scientific uncertainty.

Whether B042 (circuit QED) is premature after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits: Johansson, who opened with it first, now places it behind B044 and B024 for that reason; the chair says the instrument is the achievement and the subject is close.
Whether source-level neutrino astronomy (B019) has matured beyond the diffuse flux, per the chair's own reservation.
Whether magic-angle graphene (B020) is early because the pairing mechanism is in flux (Lindroth, chair) or established enough because replication is excellent (Danielsson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran: B042 (circuit QED) is his own field and he opened with it first; he states he should recuse from any decision on it. He lists Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson and frequent co-author Kockum, and notes that Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. He sees no conflict for B044 or B024.
Olsson-eva: notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague; she sees no conflict because his top candidate B042 is not in her preferred configuration.

The chair (Pearce) flags field proximity to IceCube (B019) as an astroparticle experimentalist, with no documented collaboration on IceCube or optical clocks, and states that it will not affect procedure.
Eriksson flags field proximity (electronic structure, DFT and correlated electrons) to B037 and, to a lesser extent, B020, with no documented personal tie to any credited person.
Mehlig flags subject proximity (stochastic processes) to B016 without a documented collaboration, supervision or institutional tie to any credited name.
Lindroth notes professional closeness to the optical-clock field as a theoretical atomic physicist, with no documented relationship with Katori or Ye.

Olsson notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, that Johansson's B042 is not in her preferred configuration, and that she finds no conflict; Danielsson notes that his own field limits his independent assessment of B044 but reports no conflict.
questions_for_round2: B044: if the committee prefers the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio, can a citation be worded around the prediction of the time-reversal-invariant Z2 state and its discovery in HgTe quantum wells so that it neither claims the three-dimensional work nor ignores the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and does each member find that wording defensible?

B044 versus B024: how should the committee weigh the broad cross-field support for B044 stated in the round-1 files against the cleanest credit and clear maturity of B024, and which members regard an unresolved attribution gap as disqualifying rather than a limit of a three-name prize?

2016 overlap: do Lindroth and Mehlig, who say the 2016 topological prize reduces B044's novelty, hold that view for time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators specifically, and what argument or evidence would change it?

B024: can members who list it only as an alternative say whether magic-wavelength lattice trapping is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and should the citation stress invention and realisation (Lindroth, Pearce) or also name the new-physics measurements (Kroll)?

B019: is any member prepared to support a sole-laureate prize to Halzen, or is there any configuration within the supplied credit that avoids omitting the AMANDA and IceCube builders; if not, how should the chair's two-part configuration be treated?

Structure: should the committee consider a one-part prize on B044 or B024, or a two-part prize pairing them or another candidate, and which pairs would any member accept given that three laureates per part is the maximum?

Recusal: should Johansson's declared recusal on B042 and Kroll's flagged Boulder stay be recorded for the final ballot, and does any member think those flags change the weight of their stated positions on B042 or B024?

B037 and B016: Eriksson now holds B037 as an alternative and Mehlig still prefers B016; how would each respond to the Metzner and Crooks omissions, and does either intend to defend the candidate as a lead in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show two sizeable positions rather than a consensus: four members prefer B044 alone, and three include B024 (Kroll and Lindroth alone, Pearce paired with B019), while Mehlig alone prefers B016. Every other shortlisted candidate is at most a named alternative. The main disagreement appears to be how much weight to give an incomplete credit set around B044 against the clean credit of B024 and its metrology lineage, together with the question of how far the 2016 prize covers the topological theme. Only the chair's configuration includes B019, and Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll each say they cannot support a sole credit for it. This summary takes no position on the outcome.
